root_cause: The ledger-internal Service annotation is misspelled: it reads service.beta.kubernetes.io/azure-load-balancer-internal-only instead of service.beta.kubernetes.io/azure-load-balancer-internal, so AKS never treats the service as internal and provisioned it on the public load balancer.
evidence: service.yaml: annotation service.beta.kubernetes.io/azure-load-balancer-internal-only: "true" (the recognized key is azure-load-balancer-internal)
kubectl-get-svc.txt: ledger-internal is type LoadBalancer with a public EXTERNAL-IP 20.162.44.128
az-network-lb-list.json: the public load balancer kubernetes owns frontend IP 20.162.44.128 and the internal load balancer kubernetes-internal has no frontend for ledger-internal
security-scan-finding.json: SEC-2026-1042 flags public IP 20.162.44.128 against finance/ledger-internal
nsg-rules.json: inbound security rules allow only VNet traffic and deny the internet (red herring - the NSG is not how the service became public)
fix: Correct the annotation to service.beta.kubernetes.io/azure-load-balancer-internal: "true" so the service reconciles onto the internal load balancer and the public IP is released.
